The patient's 2.5-year history of severe urticaria, chronic pruritus, and refractory response to treatment are characteristic of chronic urticaria.
The patient's chronic and refractory urticaria, despite treatment with omalizumab, may suggest an autoimmune component.

The patient's skin biopsy showing dermal edema with sparse chronic inflammation and dilated blood vessels, along with positive skin patch testing, is consistent with a dermal hypersensitivity reaction.

The patient's positive skin patch testing for methylisothiazolinones and presentation of edematous, superficial wheals and plaques are consistent with methylisothiazolinone-induced contact dermatitis.
